question: Why are the phonemes up to the twenty-fifth called the knowable stop-consonants?
premises: The sequence up to the twenty-fifth has the form of the knowable.
What is knowable becomes clear and manifest.
Therefore this range is declared to have the form of stop consonants.
inference: The twenty-five stop consonants represent the clearly manifest knowable domain.
plain_english: This, having the form of the knowable and extending up to the twenty-fifth, is clearly manifest. Because it is knowable and thus clear, this much is declared to have the form of the stop consonants.
